blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.why: «The following verbs belong to the "Е" type of conjugation: думать, слушать, спрашивать … The verb лежать belongs to the "И" type of conjugation.» — DLI, Lesson 16. From Викентий Вересаев, «Состязание».
exercises.context: «The following verbs belong to the "Е" type of conjugation: думать, слушать, спрашивать … The verb лежать belongs to the "И" type of conjugation.» — DLI, Lesson 16.

exercises.why: «The perfective future consists of one word only and resembles in form the present tense. It is formed from the perfective infinitive: напишу, сделаю, получу, выучу.» — DLI, Lesson 37. From Викентий Вересаев, «Состязание».
exercises.context: «The perfective future consists of one word only and resembles in form the present tense. It is formed from the perfective infinitive: напишу, сделаю, получу, выучу.» — DLI, Lesson 37.

exercises.q: Он увидел путника, ___ (выпрямить / выпрямиться), откинул кудри с загорелого лица и радостно сверкнул зубами и белками глаз.
exercises.why: «We already know that the verbs in "-ся" may be divided into several groups … Reflexive verbs. These verbs express an action which is directed back upon the agent or subject … Reciprocal verbs. The suffix "-ся" with these verbs indicates action of two or more actors upon one another … Verbs which never occur without the ending "-ся".» — DLI, Lesson 67. From Викентий Вересаев, «Состязание».
exercises.context: «We already know that the verbs in "-ся" may be divided into several groups … Reflexive verbs. These verbs express an action which is directed back upon the agent or subject … Reciprocal verbs.…

exercises.q: Дважды-Венчанный ___ (поставить / положить / посадить / повесить) кружку и удивленно поглядел на него.
exercises.why: The verb **написать** is called perfective and expresses a single action with emphasis on its completion (either in the past or in the future, since the present tense deals only with actions in progress). — From the DLI Grammar Reference Book, Lesson 37.  ·  «Phrases meaning direction are used to denote the place where something is put ("на" + Acc., "в" + Acc., etc.)» «Literally садиться means "to seat oneself". It implies movement to a "seat" and, therefore, answers the question "куда?"» — DLI, Lessons 42, 68. From Викентий Вересаев, «Состязание».
exercises.context: The verb **написать** is called perfective and expresses a single action with emphasis on its completion (either in the past or in the future, since the present tense deals only with actions in progress).

exercises.q: Он шел искать по миру высшую Красоту, запечатленную в ___ (женский) образе.
exercises.why: «All adjectives agree in gender, number and case with the noun they modify.» — DLI, Lesson 46. From Викентий Вересаев, «Состязание».
exercises.context: «All adjectives agree in gender, number and case with the noun they modify.» — DLI, Lesson 46.

exercises.q: В ___ (грудь) учителя забился ликующий смех, но лицо осталось серьезным.
exercises.why: «Some masculine nouns take the ending -у (always with a stress) in the prepositional-locative case, i.e. after the prepositions В or НА. The same nouns have the regular ending -е after О, ОБ.» — DLI, Lesson 27. From Викентий Вересаев, «Состязание».
exercises.context: «Some masculine nouns take the ending -у (always with a stress) in the prepositional-locative case, i.e. after the prepositions В or НА. The same nouns have the regular ending -е after О, ОБ.» — DLI, Lesson 27.

exercises.q: Как будто кто-то, втайне давно ___ (любимый), неожиданно наклонился к ней и тихо-тихо прошептал:
exercises.why: Masculine adjectives of the "hard" and "guttural" types have in the nominative the ending **-ой** if stressed: **новый** — **молодой**; **русский** — **плохой**, and retain the stress on the ending throughout the declension. — DLI, Lessons 46 and 47.  ·  «Больной, раненый and знакомый are often used as adjectival nouns.» — DLI, Lesson 57. From Викентий Вересаев, «Состязание».
exercises.context: Masculine adjectives of the "hard" and "guttural" types have in the nominative the ending **-ой** if stressed: **новый** — **молодой**; **русский** — **плохой**, and retain the stress on the ending throughout the declension.

exercises.why: «The prepositional case is always used with a preposition. With the prepositions в and на it denotes a location … With the preposition о, об this case answers the questions о ком? о чём?» — DLI, Lesson 16. From Викентий Вересаев, «Состязание».
exercises.context: «The prepositional case is always used with a preposition. With the prepositions в and на it denotes a location … With the preposition о, об this case answers the questions о ком? о чём?» — DLI, Lesson 16.

exercises.q: Там, на ___ (горные перевалы), лесные поляны покрыты сплошными коврами фиалок.
exercises.why: «The prepositional case is always used with a preposition. With the prepositions в and на it denotes a location … With the preposition о, об this case answers the questions о ком? о чём?» — DLI, Lesson 16. From Викентий Вересаев, «Состязание».
exercises.context: «The prepositional case is always used with a preposition. With the prepositions в and на it denotes a location … With the preposition о, об this case answers the questions о ком? о чём?» — DLI, Lesson 16.

exercises.q: Один юноша в недоумении пожал ___ (плечи) и сказал другому:
exercises.why: «The Instrumental without С is used when an instrument or agent of the action is denoted.» — DLI, Lesson 30. From Викентий Вересаев, «Состязание».
exercises.context: «The Instrumental without С is used when an instrument or agent of the action is denoted.» — DLI, Lesson 30.

exercises.why: «The direct object of a verb with negation (with не) is often in the genitive case instead of the accusative.» «Conversely, to say 'There isn't...', 'There aren't...', we use the word нет followed by the genitive case.» — DLI, Lesson 27; Wikibooks, «Genitive case». From Викентий Вересаев, «Состязание».
exercises.context: «The direct object of a verb with negation (with не) is often in the genitive case instead of the accusative.» «Conversely, to say 'There isn't...', 'There aren't...', we use the word нет followed by the genitive case.» — DLI, Lesson 27; Wikibooks,…

exercises.q: Хоть с гору величиной нарисуй, ___ (хороший) не станет! — крикнул озорной голос.
exercises.why: The comparative degree of Russian adjectives is formed by adding "**-ее**" (sometimes shortened to "**-ей**") to the stem of the adjective: **новый** — **новее**; **красивый** — **красивее**. In both English and Russian adjectives and adverbs have three forms, which are called degrees: positive, comparative, superlative — good, better, best; fast, faster, fastest. This comparative form is the same for all genders and the plural. — From the DLI Grammar Reference Book, Lessons 80, 82.  ·  «Memorize the following irregular comparatives»: рано — раньше, поздно — позже, редко — реже, часто — чаще, близко — ближе, далеко — дальше, много — больше, мало — меньше, хорошо — лучше, плохо — хуже, легко — легче, громко — громче, долго — дольше, высоко — выше, низко — ниже, жарко — жарче, дорого — дороже. — DLI, Lesson 82. From Викентий Вересаев, «Состязание».
exercises.context: The comparative degree of Russian adjectives is formed by adding "**-ее**" (sometimes shortened to "**-ей**") to the stem of the adjective: **новый** — **новее**; **красивый** — **красивее**.

exercises.q: Он ___ (увидеть / видеть) путника, выпрямился, откинул кудри с загорелого лица и радостно сверкнул зубами и белками глаз.
exercises.why: The verb **написать** is called perfective and expresses a single action with emphasis on its completion (either in the past or in the future, since the present tense deals only with actions in progress). — From the DLI Grammar Reference Book, Lesson 37.  ·  From Викентий Вересаев, «Состязание».
exercises.context: The verb **написать** is called perfective and expresses a single action with emphasis on its completion (either in the past or in the future, since the present tense deals only with actions in progress).

exercises.q: Знаю и я, что борьба предстоит трудная и ___ (победить / побеждать) тебя будет нелегко.
exercises.why: The perfective aspect places the emphasis on the result of the action. — From the DLI Grammar Reference Book, Lesson 37.  ·  From Викентий Вересаев, «Состязание».
exercises.context: The perfective aspect places the emphasis on the result of the action.

exercises.q: ___ (радоваться / обрадоваться), сын мой! — ответствовал Дважды-Венчанный и узнал Единорога, любимого своего ученика.
exercises.why: «The imperative may be formed from both the imperfective and the perfective verbs.» — DLI, Lesson 42. From Викентий Вересаев, «Состязание».
exercises.context: «The imperative may be formed from both the imperfective and the perfective verbs.» — DLI, Lesson 42.

exercises.q: Знаю, что ___ (трудный) будет борьба, но не художник, тот, кто бы испугался ее.
exercises.why: «There is a limited number of adjectives that normally take the short form when used predicatively … The short form of an adjective can never be used as a modifier.» — DLI, Lesson 57. From Викентий Вересаев, «Состязание».
exercises.context: «There is a limited number of adjectives that normally take the short form when used predicatively … The short form of an adjective can never be used as a modifier.» — DLI, Lesson 57.

exercises.q: Но подумай: та ли эта красота, ___ (который) должна повергнуть перед собою мир.
exercises.why: «"Который" in subordinate clauses agrees in gender and number with the noun it refers to in the main sentence, but its case is determined by its function in the subordinate clause.» — DLI, Lesson 53. From Викентий Вересаев, «Состязание».
exercises.context: «"Который" in subordinate clauses agrees in gender and number with the noun it refers to in the main sentence, but its case is determined by its function in the subordinate clause.» — DLI, Lesson 53.
